limitations: The receiver SSRC is bound to the logged sender, and input PTS/RTP plus saved 20Hz cadence agree. The initial sender/receiver frame-origin correspondence still lacks independently serialized per-frame network identity.
Encoder module/class/name and lifecycle counters are running-server telemetry, not an independently attested binary hash. Python object IDs alone are not used as allocation proof.
Frames sent after the receiver recording closes are reported separately from recorded frames.
No-PLI behavior is inferred from explicit force-keyframe flags and logged events; a missing event name is not standalone proof.
No normal-speed visual approval, perceptual score, network impairment test, or concurrent-capacity claim is produced.
Normal-speed visual acceptance remains pending; no bank approved.
Native codec telemetry demonstrates adaptation without bitrate-triggered context resets; this is not proof that every visible transition is imperceptible.
Single-GPU sequential-session validation does not establish concurrent capacity.
The return bound has limited margin in some cases; no threshold was relaxed.
